findings: November explicitly separates dynamic Dashboard management, code restriction, transaction compatibility and UI order at new 9–39. An authorized Dashboard role is needed, some methods require activation, approval or invite, and some wallets such as Apple Pay require registering the domain for Elements or embedded Checkout. Connected-account settings govern direct or on_behalf_of charges. The merchant or authorized account user can toggle dynamic methods without code changes, and Stripe may enable additional defaults after notice. The Dashboard cannot add a type excluded by code. Old 8–15,23–37,39–49 and source 27,33 retain earlier compatibility/recommendation but omit the specific permission, activation, some-method registration modality and Connect distinction.

New 43–83 uses allowed_payment_method_types as the Checkout Session or PaymentIntent create request allowlist. Stripe filters to compatible methods by transaction amount, currency and customer; payment_method_types is the output subset. Out-of-list methods cannot appear even when Dashboard-enabled, and allowlist order does not set display order (new 47,85–88). Older 51–87 and source 35 used payment_method_types as request with equivalent example entries. By stable 2026-09-30.endive, the linked Intent contract documents removal as a writable parameter on PaymentIntent create/update/confirm and SetupIntent create/update, with HTTP 400 code payment_method_types_no_longer_supported. Its separate Impact section advises migration before 2026-08-26.preview, so the record does not establish the first affected Intent API version (Intent Endive lines 7–16,26–28). The separate Endive Checkout changelog documents the removal and HTTP 400 specifically on Checkout Session create (Checkout Endive lines 7–23). Earlier GA Checkout still uses the old request field per the guide, while July 29 Dahlia lines 9–21 independently date the compatible allowlist for PaymentIntents and SetupIntents. The response field remains, and the May and November Checkout Session and PaymentIntent examples remain separate versioned paths.

The July 29 Dahlia Intent changelog describes silent compatibility filtering and mutual exclusion with the legacy request list, exclusion list, automatic_payment_methods and payment_method_configuration (lines 9–21). The stable Endive Intent changelog also shows payment_method_types as a read-only resource property (lines 9–16). Preserve the Checkout Session request/response distinction separately (Checkout Endive lines 9–19).

New 35–41 adds per-transaction excluded_payment_method_types for Dashboard-managed dynamic methods, a separate approach from allowlist, and explicitly distinguishes eligible-set filtering from Checkout dynamic order and the Payment Element default/order override paymentMethodOrder (new 28–41,85–88). Scoped November dynamic guide lines 89–105 shows exclusions across named surfaces and the integration-specific wallets hash for Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link instead of that exclusion field for a PaymentIntent. May 89 describes Checkout reorders and moves low priority to overflow. November retains ordering, omits overflow and does not show individual ranking, revocation or ordering of unsupported methods.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-integration-options-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-payment-method-integration-options-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/integration-options`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/integration-options, November documents how authorized Dashboard users enable eligible methods in a dynamic integration, while integration code can further restrict the eligible set; Dashboard cannot add a method outside code. Account authorization/invite and domain registration for some wallets are prerequisites, and Connected Account settings apply to direct or on_behalf_of charges. Stripe filters by compatibility, and only then does Checkout or Payment Element order remaining methods (old raw lines 8-49 and new raw lines 9-41). The merchant’s Checkout Session/PaymentIntent create allowlist filters silently to compatible types seen in the response payment_method_types. The guide describes removal of that writable create field by stable 2026-09-30.endive. Checkout Session create has its own Endive changelog. The Intent removal changelog also points to 2026-08-26.preview in its Impact section, leaving the first affected Intent version open. Dahlia 2026-07-29 already offers the Intent allowlist, and the guide identifies the old request field for earlier GA Checkout. Dashboard dynamic exclusion is separate, and Payment Element has a presentation order override (old raw lines 51-89 and new raw lines 43-88). source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options.md captures May's five UI/API options and its manual list, but needs dates, the source’s new version gates, eligibility versus order, and corrected wallet and custom-method scope. Configuration/compatible response is distinct from payment execution.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/integration-options, November materially adds the earlier-GA, July Dahlia and September Endive request boundaries, compatible response subset, explicit Dashboard/code/eligibility/order distinctions, role/approval/domain prerequisites, Connect ownership and per-transaction exclusions. It qualifies Dashboard changes as dynamic-only, adds a BNPL row and replaces the prior advanced-only custom-method label with a scope-dependent route (old raw lines 16-37 and 43-89, new raw lines 9-88 and 90-116). Preserve May 1's five paths, older request examples, numeric 40+ marketing and priority overflow as dated language. Node-to-cURL presentation, table renames, pricing/quickstart links and reordering are presentational or navigation, while updated request parameters are substantive. Preserve the July 29 Dahlia Intent allowlist availability, stable Endive writable removal for the five named Intent endpoints, and the separate Intent Impact reference to 2026-08-26.preview without assigning a first affected Intent version. Keep Checkout Session create and its Endive 400 distinct from the named Intent error code, and preserve the compatible payment_method_types response, Checkout Session and PaymentIntent examples, and scoped custom-method product boundaries. Update source-stripe-payment-method-integration-options.md and retain May raw provenance, the root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Stripe Payment Methods concept/source route, with separate Dynamic Payment Methods, domain registration and support references.
